meta.description: Analyze Perturb-seq / CROP-seq single-cell CRISPR screens. Use when assigning guides as a mixture problem, removing non-perturbed escaper cells with Mixscape, choosing a calibrated test (SCEPTRE conditional resampling) over naive DE, quantifying effect size with E-distance, separating compositional shifts from within-state expression change, or judging whether a perturbation-prediction foundation model actually beats a baseline.

scientific_integrity.detail: All 7 outputs use real data or real citations (Dixit 2016, Datlinger 2017, Replogle 2020, Papalexi 2021, Yang 2020, Barry 2021, Squair 2021, Peidli 2024, Heumos 2026, Dann 2022, Ahlmann-Eltze 2025, Kernfeld 2025, Csendes 2025 all verified as real papers); no fabricated DOIs, p-values, or results in any executed input.

practice_boundaries.detail: Purely computational/research skill; no diagnostic, prescriptive, or patient-level claims in any of the 7 outputs; no medical disclaimer required.

methodological_ground.detail: Core prose guidance (mixture over threshold, calibrated testing over naive DE, pseudobulk over pseudoreplication, composition-vs-expression) is textbook-correct and well-cited across all inputs; the Milo code defect (Input 5) is an API/design-formula bug, not a stated methodological fallacy in the prose.

code_usability.detail: 5 of 7 inputs produced real, runnable code once the skill's own documented fallback pattern (Version Compatibility section: 'introspect the installed package and adapt') was applied; the two code defects found (Input 1/4 KeyError, Input 5 AssertionError) are real but are exactly the class of drift the skill explicitly tells the agent to expect and repair, not silent unexplained failures. Scored down in dynamic_score rather than vetoed.

functional_suitability.note: Covers all 7 promised capabilities conceptually, but the two flagship worked examples (guide mixture assignment, Mixscape via examples/pertpy_analysis.py) do not run as shipped: assign_mixture_model needs an undocumented JAX extra, and the example's pert_key columns don't exist on adata.obs as written (KeyError, confirmed by execution).

reliability.note: Excellent Common Errors table (8 symptom/cause/fix rows) gives strong error-reporting value; recoverability is weaker because the ImportError from the missing JAX extra and the Milo AssertionError are not anticipated anywhere in the text.

performance_context.note: SKILL.md is 207 lines, code kept concise, usage-guide.md and examples/ separated cleanly; E-test compute cost on realistic cell counts (~3.5 min for 100 perms here) is not flagged.

agent_usability.note: Governing Principle and decision tables are very clear; one real inconsistency found: SKILL.md's prose Mixscape snippet uses pert_key='target_gene' while examples/pertpy_analysis.py uses pert_key='gene_target' for the same real dataset -- a copy-paste of either alone, mixed with the other, breaks.

human_usability.note: Description is precise but written for domain specialists (Mixscape, SCEPTRE conditional resampling, E-distance) -- correctly targeted at its actual audience, not a general user; SKILL.md doesn't spell out concrete input-shape requirements (expected MuData/obs schema) up front, which is exactly what produced the Input 1/4 KeyError above.

security.note: No credentials, no eval/exec of raw user strings, no injection surface; this is a code-pattern skill, not a service with untrusted inputs.

maintainability.note: Clean SKILL.md / usage-guide.md / examples/ split with one responsibility each; testability is hurt because the bundled example is not runnable out of the box against pertpy's own real reference dataset, and there are no expected-output assertions anywhere in the skill.

agent_specific.note: Trigger description is precise, SKILL.md stays under 500 lines with real progressive disclosure, Related Skills section (9 entries) gives excellent composability, and the Foundation-Model Reality Check / all-NP caveats are exemplary escape hatches. Idempotency docked slightly: default seeds exist in the underlying pertpy API (mixture seed=2024, Mixscape random_state=0, Milo seed=0) but SKILL.md never calls this out, and the E-test permutation has no exposed seed at all.

inputs.label: Pseudobulk DESeq2 per replicate plus Milo to separate composition from within-state DE
inputs.note: Pseudobulk step (PseudobulkSpace.compute, RAW counts summed by (gene_target, replicate)) ran cleanly: 78 = 26 targets x 3 replicates pseudobulk samples with correct columns. Milo step failed: da_nhoods(design='~gene_target') after count_nhoods(sample_col='replicate') raised AssertionError('Values ... cannot be unambiguously assigned to each sample') -- confirmed via pertpy's own da_nhoods docstring that design covariates must be constant per sample_col-defined sample, but gene_target varies cell-by-cell within each replicate in a pooled screen. This is a real structural mismatch in SKILL.md's own worked Milo example for Perturb-seq's pooled design, not an environment quirk.

recommendations.title: Default guide-assignment method needs an undocumented JAX extra
recommendations.problem: assign_mixture_model -- the skill's stated default ('Governing Principle: a mixture problem, not a threshold') -- raises ImportError under the skill's own documented `pip install pertpy scanpy anndata`; it needs the optional `pertpy[jax]` extra (optax), never mentioned in Prerequisites.
recommendations.root_cause: pertpy made the mixture-model backend an optional JAX extra at some point before 1.3.0; SKILL.md's Prerequisites section was not updated to match.
recommendations.fix: Add `pip install 'pertpy[jax]'` (or `pip install optax`) to Prerequisites, and document assign_by_threshold's real signature (`assignment_threshold`, `output_layer`, binary cell x guide layer output, not a single obs column) as the concrete fallback.

recommendations.title: Shipped pertpy_analysis.py crashes against its own reference dataset
recommendations.problem: ms.mixscape(adata, pert_key='gene_target'/'perturbation', ...) raises KeyError because adata = mdata.mod['rna'] only carries ['nCount_RNA','nFeature_RNA','percent.mito']; the perturbation/gene_target columns live on the joined mdata.obs, not on adata.obs, confirmed by running pt.dt.papalexi_2021() directly.
recommendations.root_cause: The example was written or tested against an older pertpy/papalexi_2021 loader that auto-propagated modality-joined metadata into `.mod['rna'].obs`; the current loader keeps it on the outer MuData only.
recommendations.fix: Add one line pulling the needed columns across before the guide-assignment/Mixscape calls (`for col in [...]: adata.obs[col] = mdata.obs[col].to_numpy()`), in both SKILL.md's inline snippet and examples/pertpy_analysis.py.

recommendations.title: Milo compositional-shift example is structurally incompatible with pooled Perturb-seq design
recommendations.problem: milo.da_nhoods(mdata_milo, design='~ target_gene') after count_nhoods(..., sample_col='replicate') raises AssertionError: pertpy's own da_nhoods docstring requires the design covariate to be constant per sample_col-defined sample, but gene_target/target_gene varies cell-by-cell within each replicate in a pooled screen -- it cannot be, by construction.
recommendations.root_cause: The Milo example appears adapted from a non-pooled tutorial (condition constant per sample) without accounting for Perturb-seq's per-cell perturbation identity.
recommendations.fix: Either build one Milo pseudo-sample per (replicate x guide) before count_nhoods, or replace the worked example with a method actually compatible with per-cell design (e.g. per-target-vs-NT subset_samples contrasts, or scCODA at the guide level).

recommendations.title: scMAGeCK has no code example despite being a first-class decision-table entry
recommendations.problem: Every other method in the Method Decision Table (Mixscape, SCEPTRE, E-distance, Pseudobulk DE, Milo) gets a full worked code block; scMAGeCK gets one table row and nothing else, so an agent recommending it for high-MOI/combinatorial designs has no grounded implementation to offer.
recommendations.root_cause: scMAGeCK section was scoped as a pointer/reference only, inconsistent with the rest of the skill's pattern.
recommendations.fix: Add a minimal scMAGeCK worked example (R, scmageck_lr() or RRA) mirroring the other sections' format, or explicitly note 'no bundled example -- see scMAGeCK docs' if genuinely out of scope.

recommendations.title: SKILL.md doesn't flag sceptre's R>=4.5 requirement
recommendations.problem: install.packages('sceptre') / BiocManager::install('sceptre') is a silent no-op on R<4.5 (current CRAN release requires R>=4.5); SKILL.md's Version Compatibility section lists only 'sceptre 0.10+' with no R-version caveat, so a user on an older R gets no package and no explanation.
recommendations.root_cause: Version Compatibility section tracks package versions but not the R-version floor that gates package availability at all.
recommendations.fix: Note the R>=4.5 requirement next to the sceptre version pin, and mention explicitly that BiocManager::install silently no-ops rather than erroring when the version gate is hit.

recommendations.title: E-test permutation has no documented or exposed seed
recommendations.problem: pt.tl.DistanceTest exposes no seed/random_state parameter, and SKILL.md never instructs setting a global seed before calling it, so p-values near the 1/(n_perms+1) floor are not strictly reproducible run-to-run.
recommendations.root_cause: SKILL.md's code snippet was written for illustration and doesn't address reproducibility of the permutation step specifically.
recommendations.fix: Add `np.random.seed(...)` before the etest(...) call in the example and note it as an explicit reproducibility caveat, alongside the existing 'crushed by multiple testing' warning.
